# Independent root audit: arbitrary three-fiber small-endpoint theorem


of the unrestricted OC claim. I read the complete proof in
`candidate 1350a6f7ed8eb7d0`
and checked the following dependency chain independently.

1. The maximum-volume inscribed simplex exists and is nondegenerate.
   Replacing vertex i by x multiplies its absolute volume by
   |lambda_i(x)|, proving the asserted bounded frame. Both the continuous
   affine map and the base-linear shear preserve the mixed lattice and
   uniformly scale all fiber masses. The boundedness of A requires no
   small-diameter premise.

2. In a failing triple no individual fiber can have half the total mass.
   This yields |W-V|<a. Ordinary maximal depth of B and C tends to Gamma,
   not merely their centroid depths. After selection, their limits have
   positive volume. The independently proved continuous rigidity theorem
   therefore forces simplex limits. Maximality of the normalizing
   inscribed simplex forces the middle limit to equal the fixed standard
   simplex, rather than an unspecified larger simplex.

3. The endpoint simplices S_k need only converge in volume to the large
   limiting simplex. Their translated half-size copies lie inside the
   explicit enclosing homothety T_k^+. The determinant estimate is
   uniform in p in A_k because the simplex volume is independent of p.
   Its stated threshold for |S_k|/|T_k^+| is algebraically correct.
   Transforming barycentric functions back from T_k^+ strengthens the
   positive margin because its dilation factor is at least one. Summing
   actual indicators proves the credit count even when indices vary.

4. The endpoint cap estimate uses the actual mass ratio a/W. The
   homothetic cap volume is exactly a. Its two alternatives cover every
   tilt, including thresholds at supporting planes; the branch with a
   strictly smaller cap mass legitimately gives the strict threshold
   inequality. The robust margin is at least delta/4 under (15).

5. The proper-section continuity lemma is valid without smoothness.
   Moving planes can be identified by isometries tending to the identity.
   For a limiting proper plane there is an interior point of the body
   in that plane. Convex combinations toward it make every limiting
   section point approximable by interior section points. Hausdorff
   convergence of bodies puts compact subsets of their interiors in
   all sufficiently late bodies. This proves lower section convergence;
   boundedness proves upper convergence. Section-volume continuity then
   applies in the fixed (d-1)-space. Sequential compactness justifies
   the uniform version; no exchange over improper sections is made.

6. The middle point starts at the true centroid g_k, so its initial cap
   mass is exactly bounded below by Gamma V_k without a Hausdorff-error
   term. The prescribed translation exists because the barycentric
   gradients have just the one sum relation. Its norm bound is correct.
   In (22), the section-density error contributes at most
   zeta K_d(sqrt(d)+1)a, and the normal perturbation contributes at most
   epsilon sqrt(d)a. The chosen constants make their sum at most eta a.
   The signed coarea identity handles translations of either sign.
   Consequently the credit-dependent first-order loss cancels c_i,
   leaving cbar-eta a. Since J/N>Gamma for d>=2, the exact residual
   exceeds the unequal-volume target using |W-V|<a.

7. Outside the fixed oriented neighborhoods the standard simplex has an
   attained positive cap gap by the classical equality characterization.
   Uniform cap-volume convergence supplies a fixed fraction of this gap,
   which eventually dominates a/V. Nonzero normals are all covered.
   Purely integer caps include the full middle fiber and are separately
   bounded. Arbitrary containing caps contain their through-point parallel
   caps. The selected point is a single actual middle-fiber point.

8. A putative sequence with a/V tending to zero contradicts the proved
   eventual repair, which is exactly the sequential negation of existence
   of a dimension-only positive threshold. The proof does not claim a
   computable threshold, a rate of shape convergence, an attained mixed
   global extremizer, or any conclusion for general fiber counts.

Every nonstandard step needed for this scoped implication has a proof
in the note or in its already independently audited ordinary rigidity
dependency. The measure is ordinary d-volume on three full fibers,
summed as H_d; no intrinsic degeneracy is covered by this theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
